key_insight: This paper finds that vision-language models (VLMs) do not necessarily make text representations globally more human-aligned than comparable LLMs during natural reading. In a strictly text-only setting, multimodal training history alone does not guarantee better brain-like or human-like language processing.
problem_solved: The paper addresses whether adding vision-language training actually improves how well AI models match human language processing during natural reading, independent of any live visual input.
method: Compared tightly matched LLM and VLM pairs under a strictly text-only evaluation setup.
Isolated the effect of multimodal training history by removing online visual input and cross-modal fusion during testing.
Evaluated model representations against human-reading related alignment measures to test whether VLMs are more human-like than LLMs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that multimodal pretraining is not a guaranteed path to better human-aligned text representations. It highlights the importance of carefully controlled evaluations before assuming VLMs are superior for cognitive or reading-related modeling.

paper_title: VLMs May Not Globally Enhance Human Alignment over LLMs During Natural Reading
paper_authors: Jinzhou Wu, Zhengwu Ma, Jixing Li, Baoping Tang, Zitong Lu
